applicationProfileDefinition.en: Someone or something that can act or produce an effect.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In the context of traffic measurements, this is for example the company that carries out the measurements, or the person who perfoms the counts manually.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Section of roadway intended exclusively for bicycle traffic.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Is not part of the carriageway (the carriageway is the part of the roadarea designed for vehicle traffic), e.g. cars are not allowed to drive or station on a BicyclePath. ATTENTION: Not to be confused with bicycle lanes (part of the carriageway) or with the side lanes of the central carriageway (not part of the carriageway but on which cars may drive to avoid oncoming traffic). BicyclePaths can be adjacent to the carriageway or separate or even have their own road Lane (in the latter case they are represented by their own RoadSegment).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement to which the BicyclePath relates.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In the context of this application profile, the NetworkElement is a RoadSegment or a RoadLinkSequence. The NetworkReference also enables to specify a BicyclePath for only a part of the road or for one particular road side.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A tangible object designed to accomplish a particular task.
Function that the Device can perform in order to perform a task.
Sensor hosted by the Device.
Name of the manufacturer.
Name of the model of the Device.
Task that can be performed with the Device for which the Device was designed.
Real world object that is not a SamplingObject.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This is the actual observedObject. If direct observation is not possible, we observe a representative sample, the so-called SamplingObject. In that case, the DomainObject is the sampledObject. REMARK: This class is purely informative and needs to be substituted in practice by a class from the domain. E.g. in the domain TraficMeasurements, the DomainObject could be an instance of a RoadSegment or a Vehicle.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Class representing features of instances of any type.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This is a characteristic of the observedObject (that is, of the DomainObject or of a proxy thereof, the SamplingObject) and in principle of all instances of that type of observedObject. In the context of Traffic Measurements, this concerns characteristics such as Speed (of a Vehicle - the observed Domain Object) or Number of Vehicles (passing a Measuring Point - the observed SamplingObject - along a Road Segment - the sampled Domain Object).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of information.
Any information that is provided to a procedure for its use.
Reference to original input
Nature of the input.
Part of the carriageway limited in the longitudinal direction, intended to guide the flow of the traffic in a certain direction and with usually the width of one vehicle.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: The carriageway is the part of the roadarea designed for a Vehicle to drive over. By dividing the carriageway you get a more controlled traffic flow, firstly because the driving directions or, for example, through and turning traffic are separated and also by limiting the width so that only one Vehicle can pass through one time. Lanes are typically designated by road markings, for example a white continuous or interrupted line. NOTE: Sidewalks or BicyclePaths are not Lanes as they are not intended for a car to drive on and are therefore not part of the carriageway.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Identifier of the Lane.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: The identifier must be typed, for example, according to the scheme used to number the Lanes. For example, the DATEX II scheme where Lanes are numbered from left to right over the entire width of the road.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Nature of the Lane.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, whether it is a turning lane, a bicycle suggestion lane, a center lane, etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement to which the Lane relates.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In the context of this application profile, the NetworkElement is a RoadSegment or a RoadLinkSequence. The NetworkReference also allows you to specify Lanes for only a section of the road or for one particular road side.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of Lane.
Language in which the data is set.
Curvilinear network element that connects two positions and represents a homogeneous path in the Network. The connected positions are represented by Nodes.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: By a homogeneous path we mean a route that does not branch, for example a road between two intersections (where the intersections represent Nodes in the Network).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of direction relative to the direction of a Link or Link Sequence.
Data about data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Observations can be regarded as data and therefore data about Observations are indeed metadata. We limit ourselves here to descriptive metadata, i.e. information such as title, summary, author and keywords. Such metadata is primarily intended for identification and data catalogs.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A reference to an entity responsible for making contributions to the data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Examples of a creator include a person, an organization, or a service. To be substituted by an instance of a subclass of Agent, e.g. a Person or Organization as described by Semic-Person and W3C-Organisation.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The spatial or temporal extent of the datas.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Resp. the area or period to which the data relates.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: An entity primarily responsible for the creation of the data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Examples of a creator include a person, an organization, or a service. To be substituted by a reference to an instance of a subclass of Agent, e.g. a Person or Organization as described by Semic-Person and W3C-Organisation.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Moment or period associated with an event in the life cycle of the data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. the moment in time the data was created. To be substituted by an instance of the appropriate class/datatype, e.g. representations of an instant like Date or DateTime or of a period like time::ProperInterval (see W3C Time Ontology for more info).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Further explanation on the data

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: May include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Language of the data
Reference to an entity responsible for making the data available.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Examples of a creator include a person, an organization, or a service. To be substituted by an instance of a subclass of Agent, e.g. a Person or Organization as described by Semic-Person and W3C-Organisation.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to other data associated with this data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to nformation about rights held in and over the data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Other data from which these data are derived.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: The complete data or just a subset.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the topic of the data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Name given to the data.
The nature of the data.
Element in a Network that performs an important function therein.
Instance of any type.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: To be replaced by a suitable class or data type or by specializing the Observation class with a result of an imposed data type. These can be their own subclasses or standard specializations of the Observation class such as Measurement (where the result is a Quantitative Value, i.e. a value and a unit), Classification (with a qualitative value as a result), Count (with a result of type Integer) or even Observations resulting in a Time Series or Spatial Range. ATTENTION: More info about these standard subclasses of Observation in the application profile OSLO Observations and Measurements .

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Class representing instances of any type.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In the context of Traffic Measurements, this is the Object from which a characteristic is observed. This could be a real-world Domain Object or an approximation thereof by a Sampling Object. ATTENTION: this class is abstract, use the subclasses.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Determining the value of a certain characteristic of an Object at a certain point in time or between two points in time.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: These are estimates of the value, in other words there is a certain margin of error on the value. Examples are temperature, class, color. This is different from values that are attributed and therefore not estimates such as name or price. REMARK: For more details about this class see AP Sensors and Sampling.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Collection of one or more Observations with the same properties.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. Observations that took place at the same time or observed the same Object or were made by the same Sensor. REMARK: For more details about this class see AP Sensors and Sampling.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm, or computational method specifying how to make an Observation.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: The procedure explains which steps must be performed to obtain a reproducible result. E.g. the correct placement of an anemometer (at a specific height above the ground surface, e.g. 10m for meteorological observations). The procedures are generally intended to be applied to more than one Observation.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Sensor with which the ObservationProcedure has been or is to be carried out.
Reference to the Input required or used by the procedure.
Reference to the Output that the Procedure generates or generated.
Reference to a document that describes the ObservationProcedure.
Nature of the Observation Procedure.
Type of Observationprocedure
Any information that is generated by a procedure
Reference to original output.
Nature of the Output.
An entity that hosts other entities.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: These other entities are typically Sensors, Samplers, Actuators or other Platforms. In the context of TrafficMeasurements, we define the Device subclass as a possible basis for one or more Sensors. REMARK: For more details about this class see AP Sensors and Sampling.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm, or computational method specifying how to make an Observation, create a Sample, or make a change to the state of the world (via an Actuator).

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Refers to the manner in which Observations or Sampling are performed or Actuators are operated. In practice, it takes the form of a workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm, calculation method, etc. REMARK: For more details about this class see AP Sensors and Sampling.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Linear spatial object consisting of an ordered collection of RoadSegments, representing an unbranched continuous path in a TransportationNetwork.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Typically a route in a network, e.g. a numbered road or a public transport line in a certain direction.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: DirectedLink that is part of the LinkSequence.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Significant position in the TransportNetwork that always coincides with the start or end of a RoadSegment.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Typically an intersection of roads or the beginning or end of a road.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Location of the node.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Represented by a Point.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Object that represents a part of a RoadNetwork.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Typical examples are RoadSegments, RoadNodes, RoadLinkSequences etc… REMARK: this class is abstract, only use the subclasses.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Section of the road.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In this context it refers to longitudinal subdivisions of the road such as Lanes, BicyclePaths, etc. ATTENTION: This class is abstract, use subclasses.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Linear spatial object that describes the geometry and connectivity between two points in a RoadNetwork.
Node that is the end of the RoadSegment.
Geometry of the centerline of the RoadSegment.
Node that is the start of the RoadSegment.
A Spatial SamplingObject that takes the shape of a Curve.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In that case, a representative linear part is considered of the Object that one wants to observe. Examples are routes, boreholes, profiles, intervals, etc. The Curve often specializes in a LineString. REMARK: More info about these class in the application profile OSLO Observations and Measurements .

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Part of the Object that one wants to observe and that is representative of that Object.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This part can be physical (a Sample) or spatial (a SpatialSamplingObject). One observes a SamplingObject instead of the actual Object if the latter cannot be observed in its entirety (e.g. because exhaustive observation would be impractical). The SamplingObject, together with the Process used for observation, forms the so-called observation protocol. ATTENTION: this class is abstract, it must be specialized according to the application domain.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A SpatialSamplingObject that takes the shape of a Point.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In that case, a representative point-shaped part of the Object that one wants to observe is considered. An example is a (Measuring)Station. REMARK: More info about this class in the application profile OSLO Observations and Measurements .

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Device or Agent (including Persons or software) with which Observations are made.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Sensors generate a result based on a stimulus, i.e. a change in the environment, or based on results from other Observations. They are typically hosted by a Platform. Examples are speedometers, gyroscopes, barometers, magnetometers mounted on a smart phone. The human eye, for example, can also be regarded as a Sensor.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Device that hosts the Sensor.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: ObservationProcedure applied by the Sensor.
Location of the Sensor

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, the coordinates or the address or a reference to a measuring point or other SamplingObject. Several different types of locations can be specified (e.g. address and coordinates). If the Sensor is a measuring installation, possibly the various measuring points that are included or a descriptive polygon. NOTE: The location of the Sensor is not necessarily the position where the Observation takes place, which is primarily given by the location of the SamplingObject or DomainObject. This attribute mainly allows you to describe the positions of sensors, regardless of the measurements that take place.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: TrafficMeasurement perfomed with the Sensor.
Part of roadarea dedicated to pedestrians.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: By definition seperated from the carriageway, typically by a coping stone and elevated position.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement to which the Sidewalk relates.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In the context of this application profile, the NetworkElement is a RoadSegment or a RoadLin Sequence. The NetworkReference also allows you to specify a Sidewalk for only a section of the road or for one particular road side.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indication if a value is negative or positive.
Cohesive set of components that together perform one or more functions

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: These components can be Systems in themselves. They are Systems that realize an ObservationProcedure (typically a Sensor) or with which a Sampling procedure is carried out (e.g. a drilling rig) or they are Platforms like the Device on which the Sensor is mounted. REMARK: For more details about this class see AP Sensors and Sampling.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Direction in which traffic moves on the road.
Reference to the NetworkElement to which the TrafficDirection relates.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In the context of this application profile, the NetworkElement is a RoadSegment or a RoadLinkSequence. The NetworkReference also enables to specify the TrafficDirection for only a part of the road or one particular road side.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The trafficDirection.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This is described in relation to the direction of the geometry of the road: parallel or opposite to that direction. The direction of the geometry is determined by the order in which the coordinates follow each other.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Object from the traffic domain for which a TrafficFeature is measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: By this is meant a real-world object from traffic, i.e. a Vehicle or TrafficParticipant or a RoadSegment or similar over which traffic takes place. This does not include: TrafficSamplingObjects such as TrafficMeasurementPoints or TrafficMeasurementSections, which are the objects that sample the traffic domain. ATTENTION: This class is abstract, ie it may not be instantiated. Instead, use cubclasses such as RoadSegment, Lane, Vehicle, etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Feature  of the TrafficDomainObject or the TrafficSamplingObject that is measured and that relates to the traffic over or along that object or to its participation in traffic.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, the average speed of cars past a MeasuringPoint or the traffic intensity of bicycles on a RoadSegment, for example expressed in number of vehicles or the speed of an individual Vehicle, etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of TrafficParticipant whose TrafficFeature is measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, "Pedestrian" if one only wants to count the number of pedestrians in a measuring point. Only necessary for Traffic DomainObjects that are not themselves a TrafficParticipant but, for example, a RoadSegment or Lane, etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of a TrafficFeature.
Type of Vehicle whose TrafficFeature is measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, "Bicycle" if you only want to count the number of bicycles in a measuring point. Only necessary for TrafficDomainObjects that are not themselves a Vehicle but, for example, a RoadSegment or Lane, etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of TrafficFeature.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E;g; number of vehicles, vehicle speed etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Determining the value of a certain feature of the traffic at a certain point in time or between two points in time.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Traffic is defined as the movement of objects such as people, freight, data, etc. over modes such as land, water, air, cables. In the context of this application profile, by traffic we mean road traffic. Traffic can refer to objects that move themselves (with or without a means of transport) or objects that are transported, but also to objects over which traffic takes place. The measurement can be the determination of the value of a feature of an individual Vehicle or TrafficParticipant during its movement (e.g. its speed or license plate) or of a feature of the infrastructure such as a RoadSegment or a Lane over which the traffic moves (e.g. the traffic intensity ). TrafficMeasurements are Observations, in other words there is a certain margin of error on the value due to the measuring technique used.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to Metadata of the TrafficMeasurement.
Characteristic of the TrafficObject being observed.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: CONSTRAINT: The observedFeature must actually be a feature of the observedObject or of a (sub)part of it. Sometimes the procedure by which the values of the feature are obtained is indirect, i.e. for practical reasons one measures another feature that is a proxy for the feature that one really wants to observe. For example, to determine the TrafficIntensity on a RoadSegment, individual passes by Vehicles at a Traffic MeasuringPoint are counted.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The TrafficObject being observed.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This can be the TrafficDomainObject itself or a proxy of it, i.e. a TrafficSamplingObject. NOTE: In the latter case, one sometimes only knows after observing which real-world Object one has observed. At a Traffic Measurement Point, one does not know in advance of which Vehicles exactly one will determine the speed.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The Sensor with which the TrafficMeasurement was carried out.
Agent who carried out the TrafficMeasurement
The moment at which the result of the TrafficMeasurement was applicable.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Typically the moment at which the observation or sampling takes place. If the result is a prediction, then the phenomenon time is the moment at which this prediction should apply.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The value of the observed TrafficFeature as a result of the TrafficMeasurement.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: The result can be of any type as any TrafficFeature of any type of Traffic object can be observed. CONSTRAINT: The type of the TrafficMeasurement result must match the observed feature and the obtained value must fall within the range of it.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Extent to which the result of the TrafficMeasurement meets the requirements or expectations.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This concerns data that is specific to the TrafficMeasurement and that is complementary to the description of the procedure followed during the measurement (analysis method, Sensor used, etc., see class ObservationProcedure).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Moment at which the result of the Traffic Measurement was obtained.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Is the same as the phenomenonTime for some measurements, but can also differ, for example when performing an analysis on a measurement that was taken earlier (and usually elsewhere) or on Sensor measurements that are only processed later.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Procedure followed by the TrafficMeasurement
Collection of TrafficMeasurements with the same properties

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. measurements that took place at the same time or observed the same object or feature or were made by the same Sensor. For example, the measurements of speed, vehicle type, etc. at the same TrafficMeasurementPoint or the measurements of traffic intensity per hour on the same RoadSegment, etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: TrafficMeasurements that belong to the collection.
Reference to the Metadata of the TrafficMeasurements in the collection.
Feature that the TrafficMeasurements in the collection measure.
Object observed by the TrafficMeasurements.
Sensor with which the TrafficMeasurements in the collection were obtained.
The moment at which the result of the TrafficMeasurements in the collection was applicable.
Point at which features of passing traffic are measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This is the point along the road where, for example, the passage of Vehicles is counted and/or their speed is measured or for which any other TrafficFeature is determined that relates to the sampled TrafficDomainObject.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Shape and position characteristics of the measuring point.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Datatype of the geometry is Point.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement on or along which the TrafficMeasurementPoint is located on or that is sampled by that point.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Useful if you know along which RoadSegment the point is located and on which side of the road and at what distance from the starting point. Alternative or addition to coordinates. Also necessary to indicate which RoadSegment and on which side the Vehicles are driving whose speed is measured, for example.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates on which road section the TrafficMeasurementPoint is located on or relates to.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate on which part of the road the Vehicles or TrafficParticipants, whose characteristic is being measured, are located, for example on a certain Lane or on the BiyclePath or Sidewalk.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates which TrafficDirection the TrafficMeasurementPoint is located on or relates to.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate in which direction the Vehicles are driving of which the speed is being measured, for example.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Trajectory along the road for which the characteristics of passing traffic are measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This is a distance along the road where, for example, the average speed of Vehicles is measured (the so called fixed average speed check), or any other TrafficFeature that relates to the sampled TrafficDomainObject.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Shape and position characteristics of the measurement trajectory.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Datatype of the geometry is LineString

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement along which the TrafficMeasurementSection runs or that is sampled by that trajectory.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Useful if you know along which RoadSegment the route runs and on which side of the road and at what distance from the starting point. Alternative or addition to coordinates. Also necessary to indicate which RoadSegment and on which side the Vehicles whose speed is measured, for example, are driving.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates which section of the road the trajectory runs along or relates to.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate on which part of the road the Vehicles or TrafficParticipants, whose characteristic are being measured, are located, for example on a certain Lane or on the Bicyclepath or Sidewalk.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates which TrafficDirection the TrafficMeasuringTrajectory is located on.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate in which direction the Vehicles are driving of which the average speed is being measured, for example.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Object on which or along which traffic occurs or that is part of traffic.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: ATTENTION: This class is abstract, it must be specialized as a TrafficDomainObject or as a TrafficSamplingObject. As a Traffic DomainObject if the measurement directly relates to the object you want to observe (e.g. a RoadSegment or a Vehicle, etc.) or as a TrafficSamplingObject if the measurement is done indirectly (e.g. via a TrafficMeasuringPoint located along a RoadSegment).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to a TrafficMeasurement that took place on the observedObject.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Participant in traffic, as driver or passenger of a Vehicle or without a Vehicle, for example as a pedestrian.
Nature of the TrafficParticipant.
Type of TrafficParticipant.
Object that is representative of the object for which the TrafficFeature is measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: To be used if one cannot observe this object directly. For example, to determine the speed of a Vehicle, it is impossible to track each vehicle. Instead, one sets up a measuring point along the road to see how fast passing Vehicles are driving. Similar to, for example, traffic intensity: the passages of Vehicles are counted at a measuring point along the road and it is assumed that this figure is representative of at least the part of the road between two consecutive intersections (being the corresponding RoadSegment). ATTENTION: This class is abstract, it may not be instantiated. Use the subclasses TrafficMeasurementPoint or TrafficMeasurementSection instead.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the TrafficDomainObject to which the measurement relates and for which the TrafficSamplingObject is representative.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. the Vehicle or RoadSegment for which a TrafficFeature is determined.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Linear spatial object that describes the geometry and connectivity between two points in a TransportNetwork.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: REMARK: For more details about this class see VOC Transportnetwork.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Significant position in the TransportNetwork that always coincides with the start or end of a TransportLink.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: REMARK: For more details about this class see VOC Transportnetwork.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Property of a TransportObject.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Relates to objects such as Transpor Links, TransportNodes etc or - via LinearReference - to parts of them.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Linear spatial object, consisting of an ordered collection of TransportLinks, representing a branched continuous path in a TransportNetwork.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: REMARK: For more details about this class see VOC Transportnetwork.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Object designed to transport people or goods.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. car, bicycle, truck, bus, train, tram, ship, boat, plane etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of the Vehicle.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Not to be confused with propulsion type (fuel, electric, muscle power, etc.) or transport mode (road transport, rail transport, shipping, aviation, etc.).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of Vehicle.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. car, bicycle, step etc. or noVehicle (e.g. for Pedestrians) .

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Measurable extent of something.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. length, width etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A Link either in its positive or negative direction.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Typically used in LinkSequences, it sets the Links that make up the sequence all in the same direction.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates if the directed link agrees (positive) or disagrees (negative) with the  direction of the link.
Reference to the original Link.
Distance between two points.
The spatial or temporal extent of the data.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Spatial extent can be described indirectly by means of a reference to a Place or AdministrativeUnit or GeographicalName or some other geographical object like a Building, a Road or a CadastralParcel or directly by means of Geometry. Temporal extent can be expressed as an Interval or as an Instant by a Date or DateTime. REMARK: To be substituted by Location or TemporalEntity or more specific classes or datatypes. For spatial extent see OSLO-Generics and for temporal extent the Time Ontology. Refer to existing datasets, for example for Places the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Standard way in which information is encoded for storage in a computer file.
Shape or size of something.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. the form in which something is presented (file format, program template etc), the dimensions of an object (size, dimensions etc).

applicationProfileDefinition.en: NetworkReference where the NetworkElement referred to is a Link or LinkSequence.
Direction to which the Network Property applies relative to the direction of the geometry of the Link or Link Sequence.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the Link or LinkSequence.
Shape and position characteristics of an object.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Describes these characteristics by means of points, lines, polygons and coordinates.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The GML serialization of a geometry

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Use http://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql#gmlLiteral as datatype.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: The WKT serialization of a geometry

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Use http://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql#wktLiteral as datatype.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Information used to uniquely identify an object.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Idea is that it is a String assigned by an Organisation according to a well-defined identification system.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Link to the agent who assigned the identifier.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: To be used if the agent can be referenced by means of a uri. Use the attribute "assignedBy(String)" otherwise.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Name of the agent who assigned the identifier.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Instant the identifier was assigned.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: String used to uniquely identify the object.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Type of the string refers to the identifier (incl its version), the string itself to the actual identifier.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A 0-dimensional geometric primitive in time.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Comparable with a Point in space, but instead of a position in a spatial reference system, this is about a point on the time axis. REMARK: More info in the W3C Time Ontology.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A NetworkReference that is restricted to a section of the Link or Linksequence it references.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This section lies between the fromPosition and toPosition on the Link or LinkSequence.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Distance from the start of the Link or Linksequence until the point from where the Networkproperty applies.
Distance from the start of the Link or Linksequence until the point to where the Networkproperty applies.
A Curve with linear interpolation between Points. Each consecutive pair of Points defines a Line segment. A LineString has at least two points.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: A Curve is a 1-dimensional geometric object, defined as a sequence of points. The interpolation can take different forms (e.g. linear in the case of a Line String)

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indication of a geographical position, by using coordinates, a toponym, an address label, a reference to a place/region, a reference to an address or to a geographical object.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Use location if the applicable Class or datatype is nit yet known. Otherwise t be substituted by an instance of Place, AdministrativeUnit, GeographicalName, Address or other geographical objects like a Building, a Road or a CadastralParcel. Or to be represented by Geometry like Point, LineString, Polygon. REMARK: More info about these classes/datatypes in the application profile OSLO-Generics.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A generic weakly-typed parameter value

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: In essence, a value and the name of the type of the value. E.g.  temperature of 21 degrees Celcius (value = 21 degrees Celcius, name = temperature)

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Name of the type of the value.
The quantitative or qualitative value of the NamedValue.
Reference to the NetworkElement to which the NetworkProperty applies.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Enter your translation here

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement.
Physical storage medium on which data is or can be stored

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Examples include paper, canvas, or DVD.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: A 0-dimensional geometric object that represents a single location in coordinate space. A Point has an x-coordinate value and a y-coordinate value. Has an x-coordinate and a y-coordinate. Can also have a z-coordinate (height) and an m-coordinate (distance along a curve).
NetworkReference expressed as a point along the Link or Link Sequence to which it refers.
Distance from the start of the Link or Linksequence until the point at where the Networkproperty applies.
Component of data quality

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Describes a certain component of the data quality, e.g. PositionalAccuracy, LogicalConsistency, Completeness etc. REMARK: More info about this class in the application profile OSLO Datakwaliteit.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Abstract class for temporal objects.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: These temporal entities are temporal geometric primitives like Instant or Interval. Or they are composites of temporal primitives, for example to represent the history of a phenomenon (for example the successive periods during which the phenomenon occurred). To be used when the final temporal primitive is not yet known. REMARK: More info in ISO 19108 Geographic Information - Temporal schema. Substitution by a simpler equivalent like Data/DateTime/Time or subclasses of time:TemporalEntity from W3C Time Ontology is recommended.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: TrafficMeasurements that belong to the collection.
Identifier of the Lane.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: The identifier must be typed, for example, according to the scheme used to number the Lanes. For example, the DATEX II scheme where Lanes are numbered from left to right over the entire width of the road.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Location of the Sensor

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, the coordinates or the address or a reference to a measuring point or other SamplingObject. Several different types of locations can be specified (e.g. address and coordinates). If the Sensor is a measuring installation, possibly the various measuring points that are included or a descriptive polygon. NOTE: The location of the Sensor is not necessarily the position where the Observation takes place, which is primarily given by the location of the SamplingObject or DomainObject. This attribute mainly allows you to describe the positions of sensors, regardless of the measurements that take place.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement on or along which the TrafficMeasurementPoint is located on or that is sampled by that point.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Useful if you know along which RoadSegment the point is located and on which side of the road and at what distance from the starting point. Alternative or addition to coordinates. Also necessary to indicate which RoadSegment and on which side the Vehicles are driving whose speed is measured, for example.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the NetworkElement along which the TrafficMeasurementSection runs or that is sampled by that trajectory.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Useful if you know along which RoadSegment the route runs and on which side of the road and at what distance from the starting point. Alternative or addition to coordinates. Also necessary to indicate which RoadSegment and on which side the Vehicles whose speed is measured, for example, are driving.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Characteristic of the TrafficObject being observed.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: CONSTRAINT: The observedFeature must actually be a feature of the observedObject or of a (sub)part of it. Sometimes the procedure by which the values of the feature are obtained is indirect, i.e. for practical reasons one measures another feature that is a proxy for the feature that one really wants to observe. For example, to determine the TrafficIntensity on a RoadSegment, individual passes by Vehicles at a Traffic MeasuringPoint are counted.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Feature that the TrafficMeasurements in the collection measure.
The TrafficObject being observed.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: This can be the TrafficDomainObject itself or a proxy of it, i.e. a TrafficSamplingObject. NOTE: In the latter case, one sometimes only knows after observing which real-world Object one has observed. At a Traffic Measurement Point, one does not know in advance of which Vehicles exactly one will determine the speed.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Object observed by the TrafficMeasurements.
Indicates on which road section the TrafficMeasurementPoint is located on or relates to.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate on which part of the road the Vehicles or TrafficParticipants, whose characteristic is being measured, are located, for example on a certain Lane or on the BiyclePath or Sidewalk.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates which section of the road the trajectory runs along or relates to.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate on which part of the road the Vehicles or TrafficParticipants, whose characteristic are being measured, are located, for example on a certain Lane or on the Bicyclepath or Sidewalk.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to the TrafficDomainObject to which the measurement relates and for which the TrafficSamplingObject is representative.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: E.g. the Vehicle or RoadSegment for which a TrafficFeature is determined.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates which TrafficDirection the TrafficMeasurementPoint is located on or relates to.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate in which direction the Vehicles are driving of which the speed is being measured, for example.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Indicates which TrafficDirection the TrafficMeasuringTrajectory is located on.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: Alternative or supplement to geometry or network reference. Also necessary to indicate in which direction the Vehicles are driving of which the average speed is being measured, for example.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of TrafficParticipant whose TrafficFeature is measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, "Pedestrian" if one only wants to count the number of pedestrians in a measuring point. Only necessary for Traffic DomainObjects that are not themselves a TrafficParticipant but, for example, a RoadSegment or Lane, etc.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Reference to a TrafficMeasurement that took place on the observedObject.

applicationProfileDefinition.en: Type of Vehicle whose TrafficFeature is measured.

applicationProfileUsageNote.en: For example, "Bicycle" if you only want to count the number of bicycles in a measuring point. Only necessary for TrafficDomainObjects that are not themselves a Vehicle but, for example, a RoadSegment or Lane, etc.
